Fixes #321025

Aligns the Customizations inner panel's right and bottom inset with the compact modal controls. The associated widget layout dimensions are updated by the same amount so list and model content continue to use the full available panel area.

## Before / After

Both screenshots use the Light 2026 theme and show the top-right corner of the Customizations modal.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: the inner panel has a wider right inset than the modal controls](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a5274ed2-cfd1-4636-8d27-21d09ba62b65) | ![After: the inner panel right inset aligns with the modal controls](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f52c1100-3812-4a3c-8ecf-9eb9cebef585) |

## Validation

- Passed `npm run build-fast -- --client-only`.
- Passed `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationManagementEditor.ts`.
- Passed `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/test/browser/componentFixtures/sessions/aiCustomizationManagementEditor.fixture.ts`.
- Passed `npm run stylelint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/media/aiCustomizationManagement.css`.
- Passed `git diff --check`.
- Verified the live modal in dark and light themes at wide and constrained sizes. The inner panel and close control have matching 9px effective edge insets (8px spacing plus the 1px modal border), with no viewport overflow.
- Verified the LocalHarness, AgentsTabNarrow, WelcomePageNarrow, and DiscoverSearchResultsNarrow Component Explorer fixtures in dark and light themes. All targeted fixtures rendered without errors and were stable across repeated captures.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the Customizations editor, switch among Agents/MCP/Plugins/Models/Tools, and resize the editor or sidebar sash
Scenarios.CriticalPath: EditorPane.layout synchronously invokes SplitView.layout, whose existing content-view callback lays out the currently visible list/model widget. The diff changes each widget's supplied width/height by 8px but adds no layout invocation, geometry read, or critical-path stage.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Resize/layout event frequency and the number of visible virtualized rows. Call cardinality remains one layout call per existing visible widget per outer layout; the 8px viewport increase can expose at most a boundary row rather than changing scaling with total collection size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single-threaded synchronous DOM/widget layout, exactly as before; no new queue, scheduler, or concurrent work is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache key, cache population, invalidation, coalescing, or cold/warm behavior changes on this path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the changed SplitView callback and outer layout call path: the same widget layout methods execute at the same points with only numeric viewport arguments changed.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual widget layout duration depends on visible content and platform, but the diff does not increase invocation count and only changes dimensions by 8px.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Existing synchronous layout work remains on the same critical path and at the same cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render the Welcome/Discover surface, including narrow 550px search-result fixtures and marketplace pagination near the viewport threshold
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Outer editor layout synchronously lays out the welcome/discovery page and virtualized result list. The CSS padding reduction increases available right/bottom space by 8px; discovery then performs its pre-existing continuation-threshold check after layout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query one marketplace catalog page when the existing virtual-list continuation threshold is reached
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most the pre-existing single scheduled continuation at a time; page count remains controlled by catalog cursors and filters, not by the changed padding.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same layout method, threshold check, scheduler, cancellation guard, and marketplace query already ran before the diff with an 8px smaller viewport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial/search rendering can await marketplace data as before; the changed CSS may shift an edge threshold by 8px but does not add a query stage or sustained extra request multiplicity.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Viewport size, rendered virtual-list height, and marketplace page count. The threshold remains three result rows and the request scheduler/load guard remain unchanged; an 8px viewport shift can only move an already-near-threshold continuation earlier, not create per-item requests or systematic fan-out.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Continuation remains coalesced by one RunOnceScheduler and guarded by loading/next-page state, with one cancellable marketplace request active at a time.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Browse results continue to use the existing per-source browseCatalogCache; search pagination and cancellation behavior are unchanged. The fixture expectation changes only the asserted rendered width and does not alter runtime caching.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the traced layout-to-pagination path and request guards; low evidence of any meaningful cost increase because request scheduling/cardinality logic is untouched.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact marketplace result heights can place a viewport near the continuation threshold, but there is no realistic scaling mechanism that turns the 8px geometry change into additional fan-out or concurrency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The changed dimensions provide intended panel area without adding boundary operations, defeating virtualization, or increasing effective concurrency.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all three changed files and traced the resize/list-layout and welcome/discovery critical paths. The PR changes padding and matching widget dimensions from 16px to 8px plus fixture expectations; it introduces no additional work frequency, retained state, eager initialization, or expensive-boundary fan-out.
